title: Define drift SLI and configure monitoring + alerts for Cost Model API
creator: Ethan Park
description:
We need a single, auditable drift SLI definition for the Standard Cost Model initiative, plus a monitoring pipeline that continuously compares predicted (cost-model outputs) vs observed (infra spend / GPU-seconds-derived cost) and alerts when drift exceeds thresholds. This is required before Console flips cost breakdowns broadly and before Finance treats standard cost outputs as a reliable unit-econ primitive.

Context: We already saw a drift alert fire due to telemetry lag (see incidents thread 1769032199). This ticket formalizes drift semantics, adds lag-awareness + volume guardrails, and ships actionable dashboards + paging rules.

Deliverables:
- Drift SLI definition (v1) with explicit formulae, inclusion/exclusion rules, and windowing/lag policy.
- Scheduled drift monitoring job/pipeline emitting Prometheus metrics (bounded cardinality).
- Grafana dashboard + alert rules (warn/page) with runbook links and clear next steps.

Non-goals:
- Perfect cost reconciliation to invoices (billing system of record remains separate).
- Per-customer drift alerts at high cardinality (we will do top-K / aggregate-first in v1).

Primary stakeholders: Rafael Mendes (SRE), Logan Wright / Mei Lin (Telemetry), Ethan Park (API), Laura Bennett / Rishi Malhotra (FP&A).
acceptance_criteria:
- Drift SLI v1 is documented and reviewed by SRE + Telemetry + Finance (written definition + examples).
- Drift pipeline runs on schedule in prod and emits:
  - drift_ratio metrics for 1h/6h/24h windows
  - telemetry_lag_seconds + data_freshness indicators
  - sample sizes (request_count / token_count / gpu_seconds) for gating
- Alerting:
  - P0 page when sustained high drift and volume gate is met
  - P1 warning when drift elevated but below page threshold
  - Separate alert for telemetry lag (to avoid false positives)
- Dashboard provides drill-down to top contributors with bounded series (top-N + “other”).
- Runbook section updated with “drift” triage steps + common causes (telemetry lag, schema mismatch, runtime metric regression, overhead allocation changes).
- Backtest on last 14 days shows alert thresholds don’t flap (documented).
sli_definition_v1:
Name: cost_model.drift (v1)

Goal: quantify how far Cost Model predicted cost deviates from observed infrastructure-derived cost over a fixed reporting window, after applying the same allocation policy.

Definitions:
- Predicted cost (P): Sum of cost-model ‘request_attributable_total_usd’ over the window, computed from cost-model primitives (prefill/decode, cache, batch efficiency, quantization profile) using schema version pinned per environment.
- Observed cost (O): Infra-derived cost over the same window, mapped to the same attribution scope:
  - v1 uses GPU-seconds * effective_usd_per_gpu_second by cluster/SKU/region/deployment_mode
  - excludes non-GPU line items and one-time credits
  - includes request-attributable overhead per the agreed overhead allocation policy (see Finance thread/email; implemented as overhead_multiplier or overhead_usd bucket)

Drift ratio:
- drift_ratio = (P - O) / max(O, O_floor)
- O_floor is to avoid division noise; v1 O_floor = $50 per window (configurable).

Windowing & freshness:
- Compute over rolling windows: 1h, 6h, 24h.
- Apply a data-lag offset: exclude the most recent 2 hours from both P and O when computing drift (configurable) unless telemetry freshness guarantees improve.

Gating (to reduce noise):
- Only emit window-level drift alerts when:
  - request_count >= 10,000 OR token_count >= 50M OR observed_cost >= $200 for that window (thresholds configurable by env)

Dimensions (bounded):
- Always emit global (no dimensions) drift.
- Emit limited breakdown by:
  - deployment_mode (hosted/dedicated/private)
  - region
  - hardware_sku
  - model_id (top 10 by observed_cost in the window) + “other”
- No per-tenant/customer dimension in v1.

Interpretation guidelines:
- Positive drift_ratio means predicted > observed (we are over-attributing).
- Negative drift_ratio means predicted < observed (we are under-attributing).
implementation_plan:
1) Finalize SLI semantics + Finance alignment (owners: Rafael, Laura, Rishi)
- Confirm overhead allocation treatment in O vs P so we’re not comparing apples to oranges.
- Document what is excluded (CPU, storage, credits) for v1.

2) Data sources + joins (owners: Mei, Logan, Thomas)
- Predicted P: use telemetry-derived request aggregates produced by cost-model drift job (not live request path).
- Observed O: consume daily/hourly infra cost export or GPU-seconds accounting table (whichever is already used for internal unit econ).
- Add freshness checks + telemetry lag metric.

3) Job + metrics emission (owners: Rafael)
- Implement scheduled job (hourly) that computes drift for windows ending at T-2h.
- Emit Prometheus metrics:
  - cost_model_drift_ratio{window="1h",...}
  - cost_model_observed_cost_usd{window,...}
  - cost_model_predicted_cost_usd{window,...}
  - cost_model_drift_gated{reason="low_volume"|"stale_data"|"ok"}
  - cost_model_telemetry_lag_seconds
- Enforce series limits: topK selection, aggregate remainder into “other”.

4) Dashboard + alerts (owners: Allison + Rafael)
- Add Grafana dashboard panels:
  - Global drift time series (1h/6h/24h)
  - Telemetry lag + job success
  - Top contributors table for model_id/hardware_sku/region
  - Correlate with cost-model API error rate + schema version distribution
- Alerting rules:
  - Page: |drift_ratio| > 0.10 for 2 consecutive 1h windows AND volume gate met AND telemetry fresh
  - Warn: |drift_ratio| > 0.05 for 3 consecutive 1h windows (same gates)
  - Telemetry lag page: telemetry_lag_seconds > 3h for 2 consecutive evaluations

5) Backtest & threshold tuning (owners: Rafael + Logan)
- Run job in shadow for ~1 week, compare alert firing to known changes (runtime deploys, schema changes).
- Tune O_floor and volume gates if needed.

6) Runbook updates + handoff (owners: Rafael)
- Update incident runbook with drift triage steps and links to dashboard.
- Confirm oncall rotation + escalation to Telemetry/Runtime/Platform depending on root cause.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: false positives due to telemetry lag or partial backfills.
Mitigation: explicit lag offset (T-2h), freshness metric, and gating so drift alerts require fresh data.

Risk: cardinality explosion (model_id x region x sku).
Mitigation: topK + other bucketing; hard caps in job; no per-tenant dimension v1.

Risk: comparing predicted request-attributable cost to observed spend that includes unrelated overhead.
Mitigation: implement the same overhead allocation policy in both P and O (or emit both ‘request_attributable’ and ‘allocated_total’ drift; v1 is allocated_total drift).

Risk: silent drift masked by gates.
Mitigation: always emit ungated global metrics for dashboard visibility, but only page on gated conditions; add a weekly report for low-volume dims.

Risk: schema version migrations cause step changes.
Mitigation: include schema_version label in drift job output at global level; add alert suppression during planned migrations; coordinate with release train (Connor).
notes_for_oncall:
When drift alert fires:
1) Check telemetry freshness + drift job success.
2) Check if a recent deploy occurred (runtime instrumentation, cost-model schema/service) and whether schema_version distribution changed.
3) Compare dimensions: is drift isolated to one hardware_sku, region, or model_id?
4) If drift aligns with a single model_id, validate runtime-exported prefill/decode split + KV cache metrics (known source of regressions).
5) If drift is broad across all dims, check infra cost export delay or allocation policy changes.
6) Use runbook section ‘Cost drift SLI’ and escalate:
- Telemetry lag / ingestion: Logan Wright / Mei Lin
- Runtime metrics regression: Sofia Ivanova / Omar El-Sayed
- Cost-model logic/schema change: Ethan Park
- Allocation policy / reporting window questions: Laura Bennett / Rishi Malhotra
comments: 2026-01-20 — Rafael Mendes: Drafted initial drift formula proposal. Key open question: do we compare against GPU-seconds-derived cost or cloud billing export (billing export has 24h latency). Leaning GPU-seconds for v1 to get 1h/6h windows; Finance ok as long as the USD rate table is versioned and auditable.

2026-01-23 — Laura Bennett: Confirmed Finance wants drift measured against allocated cost (includes request-attributable overhead per policy), not bare GPU cost. Also requested that we always expose both components in the dashboard to explain deltas during month-end close.

2026-01-29 — Logan Wright: Telemetry lag is still ~60–120m at p95 during peak. Please bake in a fixed offset (2h) and a freshness check; otherwise we will page on ‘missing data’ again like the 1769032199 incident.

2026-02-03 — Allison Grant: For alert hygiene, gate on both $ and volume; use an O_floor so we don’t page on a $5 window. Also please add a ‘job last success timestamp’ metric so oncall can quickly distinguish ‘pipeline down’ vs ‘real drift’.

2026-02-11 — Ethan Park: Noted that schema migrations can shift P. Suggest adding schema_version label at least at global level, and annotate the Grafana dashboard via deploy markers during planned rollouts (Connor coordinating).

2026-02-18 — Rafael Mendes: Implemented job in staging with top-10 model bucketing + other. Next: wire to prod metrics and create alert rules behind a disabled-by-default toggle until we backtest 7 days.
